obernants.approximation_semantics: Source-derived relation with finite tests; not universal verification.
obernants.assumptions: Rust slice, integer and allocation semantics; standard comparison sort oracle.
obernants.domain: Finite integer slices and ordinary terminating execution including allocator outcomes.
obernants.observation_scope: One sort call or explicitly scoped internal pass.
obernants.operator: For observations (input, allocator outcome, Result, output), exclude nonascending success, changed length or multiset, mutation on reserve error, or failure after any byte pass. Internal pass observations exclude decreasing digit order or reversal within equal-digit source subsequences.

obernants.approximation_semantics: Source-derived relation with finite tests; not universal verification.
obernants.assumptions: Rust slice, integer and allocation semantics; standard comparison sort oracle.
obernants.domain: Finite integer slices and ordinary terminating execution including allocator outcomes.
obernants.observation_scope: One sort call or explicitly scoped internal pass.
obernants.operator: Given successful sorted output y, compatible original inputs are all permutations of its multiset; allocation must succeed unless len<2. Err admits the unchanged input and failed reserve. For an internal digit-pass result, predecessors are shuffles of digit subsequences preserving order within each digit. Sorting is not injective; no unique original ordering is claimed.

obernants.assumptions: Rust slice, integer and allocation semantics; standard comparison sort oracle.
obernants.domain: Finite integer slices and ordinary terminating execution including allocator outcomes.
obernants.observation_scope: One sort call or explicitly scoped internal pass.
obernants.operator: S(S(x))=S(x). Each byte pass preserves every digit subsequence. Tests use distinct scalar values sharing selected byte keys to observe internal pass stability; scalar full-sort equality cannot demonstrate attached payload stability.

obernants.approximation_semantics: Source-derived conditional relation with bounded correspondence checks; no universal verification.
obernants.assumptions: Valid Rust slices, representable arithmetic where stated, and allocator outcomes held fixed where required.
obernants.domain: Private byte_pass with byte 0..7, equal source/destination lengths, arbitrary u64 values.
obernants.observation_scope: One whole sort or explicitly scoped internal state transition.
obernants.operator: For fixed byte b and digit-sorted y, P_b(x)=y iff for every digit d the subsequence of x with digit d equals that of y in order. Thus predecessors are interleavings of fixed digit subsequences, not arbitrary multiset permutations. Distinct values [0x300,0x100,0x201,0x001] give six accepted shuffles at byte zero; reversing a same-digit pair is rejected.

obernants.approximation_semantics: Source-derived conditional relation with bounded correspondence checks; no universal verification.
obernants.assumptions: Valid Rust slices, representable arithmetic where stated, and allocator outcomes held fixed where required.
obernants.domain: Eight internal passes, k in 1..8, successful scratch allocation and distinct or repeated u64 scalars.
obernants.observation_scope: One whole sort or explicitly scoped internal state transition.
obernants.operator: After k stable passes in increasing byte significance, output is the stable ordering of original input by its low 8k bits. At k=8 this is full unsigned order; using a full-width mask avoids shifting by 64. Reversing pass order or reversing equal-digit source subsequences invalidates the inductive step. All eight stages are compared against an independent stable key sort.

obernants.approximation_semantics: Source-derived conditional relation with bounded correspondence checks; no universal verification.
obernants.assumptions: Valid Rust slices, representable arithmetic where stated, and allocator outcomes held fixed where required.
obernants.domain: Finite u64 slices, bounded strictly increasing transformations, successful whole-sort calls.
obernants.observation_scope: One whole sort or explicitly scoped internal state transition.
obernants.operator: S(f(x))=f(S(x)) for f strictly increasing on the finite support with representable u64 images and successful allocations. The checked affine map 257v+19 is observed; wrapping addition on [0,MAX] is a countermodel when representability is dropped. This is a full-sort law, not a law that byte partitions commute with arbitrary relabeling.

obernants.approximation_semantics: Source-derived conditional relation with bounded correspondence checks; no universal verification.
obernants.assumptions: Valid Rust slices, representable arithmetic where stated, and allocator outcomes held fixed where required.
obernants.domain: Whole-call Result and input/output observations including allocator outcomes; valid allocatable Rust slices.
obernants.observation_scope: One whole sort or explicitly scoped internal state transition.
obernants.operator: Lengths zero and one succeed without reservation. For n>=2 the sole fallible reservation precedes every pass and copy; Err therefore has unchanged input and a failed reservation as compatible antecedent. Scratch length and requested capacity are n u64 elements (the allocator may reserve more) and counts use 256 usize slots per pass. No public budget parameter or allocator failure injection exists; exact allocator feasibility cannot be inferred from n alone.

obernants.approximation_semantics: Source-derived conditional relation with bounded correspondence checks; no universal verification.
obernants.assumptions: Valid Rust slices, representable arithmetic where stated, and allocator outcomes held fixed where required.
obernants.domain: Internal valid byte passes; byte index 0..7 and destination length n.
obernants.observation_scope: One whole sort or explicitly scoped internal state transition.
obernants.operator: Counts sum to n and prefix starts partition destination into digit intervals [sum_{e<d}H[e],sum_{e<=d}H[e]). Left-to-right source traversal advances each cursor once per occurrence, preserving its subsequence. Disjoint intervals imply no dropped or duplicated values. Whole-sort scalar equality cannot establish stability of attached records absent from this API.
